metadata.title: Advanced GitHub Concepts 🧠
metadata.description: Test your knowledge of advanced GitHub workflows and Git concepts.

metadata.title: Repository Analytics 📊
metadata.description: Learn to analyze repository statistics and understand project activity.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the issue tracker in a GitHub repository?
questions.optionA: To list all contributors to the project
questions.optionB: To track bug reports, feature requests, and project discussions
questions.optionC: To store documentation and project guidelines
questions.optionD: To manage pull requests and merges
questions.explanation: The issue tracker is the central hub for project discussions, bug reports, and feature requests.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a pull request on GitHub?
questions.optionA: A way to propose changes to a repository, allowing for code review and discussion before integration
questions.optionB: A method of archiving issues and marking them as resolved
questions.optionC: A feature used for backing up repository data to a different server
questions.optionD: A section where repository settings and configurations are modified
questions.explanation: Pull requests allow contributors to propose changes that can be reviewed before being merged.

questions.question: Why would you fork a repository on GitHub?
questions.optionA: To permanently delete it from your account
questions.optionB: To merge two different repositories into one
questions.optionC: To create a personal copy where you can experiment and make changes without affecting the original
questions.optionD: To mark it as one of your favorite projects
questions.explanation: Forking creates a personal copy for experimentation without affecting the original project.

questions.question: What information is typically found in a README file of a GitHub project?
questions.optionA: The project's history and commit logs
questions.optionB: A guide on how to contribute, along with an overview of the project
questions.optionD: All the issues that have ever been reported
questions.explanation: README files provide project overview and contribution guidelines for new contributors.

questions.question: How can understanding who has contributed the most to a project be useful?
questions.optionA: It ensures that you get paid for your contributions
questions.optionB: It prevents other people from making changes to your code
questions.optionC: It lets you change the project's license to your preference
questions.optionD: It helps identify the project's most active users and potential people to reach out to for guidance
questions.explanation: Knowing top contributors helps identify who to ask for help or guidance on the project.

T6.accept:
### 🧠 Quest 1 Quiz

Answer the following questions to test your knowledge of the GitHub contribution process.

**Question 1:** What is the primary purpose of the issue tracker in a GitHub repository?

A) To list all contributors to the project
B) To track bug reports, feature requests, and project discussions
C) To store documentation and project guidelines
D) To manage pull requests and merges

**Question 2:** Which statement best describes a pull request on GitHub?

A) A way to propose changes to a repository, allowing for code review and discussion before integration
B) A method of archiving issues and marking them as resolved
C) A feature used for backing up repository data to a different server
D) A section where repository settings and configurations are modified

**Question 3:** Why would you fork a repository on GitHub?

A) To permanently delete it from your account
B) To merge two different repositories into one
C) To create a personal copy where you can experiment and make changes without affecting the original
D) To mark it as one of your favorite projects

**Question 4:** What information is typically found in a README file of a GitHub project?

A) The project's history and commit logs
B) A guide on how to contribute, along with an overview of the project
C) Personal information about the contributors
D) All the issues that have ever been reported

**Question 5:** How can understanding who has contributed the most to a project be useful?

A) It ensures that you get paid for your contributions
B) It prevents other people from making changes to your code
C) It lets you change the project's license to your preference
D) It helps identify the project's most active users and potential people to reach out to for guidance

**Important:** Please provide answers in the format [x,x,x,x,x] where each letter corresponds to your answer for each question.

**Example:** If you think the answers are A, C, B, D, E, type: [a,c,b,d,e]

**Note:** There is only one attempt allowed!
